title: Guardian Commander Yvette
dek: A Guardian commander proud of a lifetime guarding Prima’s sacred ward. Her port is robbed, her corps remembers its dead, and later testimony about her own murder leaves a discrepancy the surviving scenes do not resolve.

facts.Later report: 29 March 2026 · the Guardians refer to her murder; chronology unresolved

sources: Main quest-RP · selected primary scenes; anchors below
Supplied deep dossier · interpretation checked against quest evidence
body:
Yvette’s command is attached to a corps with its own duties and losses. At a private military port, she is responsible for access, supplies and soldiers whose loyalty she defends. Her history gives institutional service a personal cost without assigning her every guard action on Prima.

December 2024 · a corps on a schedule

She challenges the visitors’ presence, explains that her people are on a tight schedule and directs soldiers loading supplies with military hand signals. Visitors may inspect, but not touch. Those choices establish practical command through coordination and boundaries.

Navi’s claim that the visitors serve the gods does not immediately win her trust. Yvette describes her service as a lifetime’s duty and responds emotionally to the possibility that others have been given a role her people have long borne. Her pride belongs to work and responsibility, not simply to rank.

Directness and fallibility

In the same scene, narration presents her as inexperienced at deception. That supports a moment of visible awkwardness; it does not prove she has never lied in any circumstance or supply a complete personality diagnosis.

A badger steals the keys from her belt. She notices the theft, orders the animal found and tells guards to detain its owner; guards move to detain Sparrow while others search. Her response shows both a security failure and an attempt to restore control. It is neither proof of general incompetence nor an independent finding that her accusation is just.

The encounter also shows how differently duty can look to a commander and to adventurers. Yvette sees trusted soldiers and an obligation. The visitors’ confidence in their own purpose does not automatically answer her concern about what they will do at her port.

February 2026 · the soldiers’ graves

In a later investigation, she insists that her corps can conduct its own inquiry. Her estimate of the attackers remains testimony, rather than a settled investigation result. She offers to take the visitors to her soldiers’ graves.

Yvette remembers the deaths of people who served in the corps. Her offer helps explain her earlier insistence on loyalty: she continues to feel responsible for those soldiers.

The limits of the command record

Yvette is a Guardian commander connected to Prima. These scenes do not establish that she commands Pristinia’s town militia, answers to every Elder or possesses a general legal authority over all adventurers. Her appointment, formal chain of command, complete service history and status after the reviewed February scene remain unresolved.

A lifetime’s duty meets unexpected replacements

Yvette tells Navi that her corps guards Prima’s Shard against Death and knows no other calling. She is skeptical that the rowdy-looking visitors share the same purpose. When Navi says Cala and Nuru summoned them, Yvette becomes upset: she has given her life to this work and hears that the gods have handed her role to strangers.

The exchange reveals pride and hurt rather than a completed transfer of command. She still directs her soldiers, describes the tree’s beauty and treats their equipment as tools given for the job. Her corps has its own service, obligations and cost. A visitor’s divine calling does not automatically answer the concerns of someone already guarding the island.

The keys, the chest and the escape

The loss of Yvette’s keys becomes part of a larger attack rather than an isolated embarrassment. She holds Sparrow responsible for the badger and orders his detention. The guards split their attention, the ship is sabotaged and Amity starts dragging the heavy chest away. When Sparrow threatens to complain to Scribonia, Yvette answers that she will tell Cala they are stealing from her.

As fighting spreads, the guards abandon the chase after the badger to respond to the stolen chest. Farkur prepares the escape vessel, and the party hauls its burden aboard. The narrator confirms their escape while Yvette cries that it is sacrilege. Her attempt to maintain the port’s rules ends with the people she distrusted leaving with what her corps was protecting.

The scene records individual acts and a successful theft. It does not make every visitor identical in knowledge or responsibility. Farkur later gives his own account of what he understood and why he failed to report it; the commander’s accusation and the later hearing remain connected without replacing either with his version alone.

The graves, a later death report and an unresolved chronology

In the later visit to the Guardians, Horgrith and Moliena still speak of theft, murder and an unpaid obligation. Yvette speaks directly, insists that her people can investigate their own holy ward and offers to take Gregory to her soldiers’ graves. A wanted poster supplies faces to accompany the accusation. The visitors’ request for cooperation meets an institution that remembers an injury.

At Farkur’s subsequent hearing, Horgrith explicitly asks about Commander Yvette’s murder. Farkur admits preparing the escape ship while denying that he went ashore or attacked anyone. Moliena accepts his account of his intentions and presses no charges against him, while continuing to describe the theft and killings as a betrayal. Horgrith later refuses renewed cooperation.

The surviving scenes leave a chronological discrepancy: Yvette is a speaking participant in the quest posted 15 February 2026, while the hearing posted 29 March 2026 names her as a murder victim in connection with the earlier ship affair. The reviewed record does not show her death or return, or establish that the name used in that earlier visit was mistaken. Both appearances of the record remain visible pending clarification. Her personal fate and the date or nature of any death must not be filled in from the accusation alone.

profile.personality: Direct, proud of her corps and wounded by the thought that divine newcomers could replace its lifetime of service. She tries to restore order after the stolen keys, defends the soldiers’ loyalty and remembers their graves. A narrated difficulty with deception is a scene observation, not a universal guarantee that she cannot lie.
profile.achievements: Commands a corps at a private military port, coordinates loading and guards access to supplies and a sacred ward. Attempts to stop the theft and later offers to show the soldiers’ graves. A later hearing calls her a murder victim, while an intervening quest gives her dialogue; no complete death or return account is established.
profile.relationships: Her soldiers are the people she calls loyal and continues to mourn. Navi questions her calling, Sparrow becomes the target of her detention order, and the escaping party defeats her control of the port. Farkur later confesses to enabling the escape, while Horgrith and Moliena keep the institutional grievance alive.
